request.user:
Subject: Zoology
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

Which tissue is present in the lining of small intestine?
(A) Epithellial tisue
(B) Connective tissue
(C) Nervous tissue
(D) Muscular tissue

result.working: The inner lining (mucosa) of the small intestine is formed by simple columnar epithelium with microvilli (brush border) and goblet cells. Connective, muscular and nervous tissues are present in the deeper layers (submucosa, muscularis, plexuses), not in the lining itself. So option A is correct.
result.note: Option A is misspelled ('Epithellial tisue') but clearly means epithelial tissue.
